beats.narration: On Wed 11 Nov 2026, Tom Bradley calls to claim on his income protection. He fell from a ladder on 14 Oct, tore his rotator cuff and had surgery on 21 Oct. Kylie joins as his support person, with his written authority.
Olivia's agent extracts the claim notification and Kylie's authority, and flags financial stress: Tom is self-employed, and his surgeon expects four to six months off work.
Olivia opens case REQ-20261111-LIF004 (CL-102265) and routes it to Claims.

Ben's agent checks Harbourline Life policy HL-23051877: $7,000 a month insured, a 30-day waiting period, benefits to age 65. It pays the lesser of the insured benefit and 70% of Tom's average monthly earnings in the 12 months before the injury: $96,000 a year is $8,000 a month, and 70% is $5,600. It explains why it isn't $7,000.
Felix's agent checks the BAS, the profit and loss statement and the surgeon's report: all legit.

Theo reviews the case for a vulnerable client, approves lodging the claim and asks Amelia to call Tom personally before the letter. A note for Amelia, not advice: Tom's $7,000 is more than his recent income supports, which she may look at in his next review.

Ben's agent raises the Teams approval and lodges the claim with Harbourline Life on 12 Nov. Harbourline accepts it on 19 Nov at $5,600 a month, from 13 Nov 2026 after the waiting period, paid monthly in arrears: the first payment is about 13 Dec.
Cara's agent sends Tom a plain-English letter: why the benefit is $5,600 and not $7,000, when it is paid, and that it is taxable income.

result.headline: Claim accepted at $5,600 a month
result.summary: Outcome: PARTIALLY APPROVED — claim accepted at $5,600 a month, not the $7,000 insured, because the benefit follows his earnings in the 12 months before the injury.
